headline: India: From school to wedding house: Myanmar military airstrikes leave over 35 civilians dead
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- India: From school to wedding house: Myanmar military airstrikes leave over 35 civilians dead.
- Africa: Saudi coalition shoots down Houthi cruise missile fired toward Riyadh.
- Persian Gulf Region: Pompeo predicts US blockade will push Iran to escalate, reigniting Israel, US strikes on regime.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: ‘We can’t intercept them all’ - Chang warns of Haitian gangsters eyeing Jamaica with gaps in coastal security.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: ‘We can’t intercept them all’ - Chang warns of Haitian gangsters eyeing Jamaica with gaps in coastal security.
WESTERN BUREAU: National Security Minister Dr Horace Chang has raised concerns about the vulnerability of Jamaica’s coastline, disclosing that more than a dozen gangsters seeking to flee Port-au-Prince have identified Jamaica as a possible destination.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: US ICE releases Argentine acrobats after 20 days of arrest.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 23 hours ago: US ICE releases Argentine acrobats after 20 days of arrest.
Agustín Baccega and Gustavo Romanello, a couple from Córdoba, were released on bail. One was seen with an ankle monitor La entrada US ICE releases Argentine acrobats after 20 days of arrest se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian Army Intercepts Over 1.2K Ukrainian Drones in Latest Nighttime Air Barrage.
- The Moscow Times, 9 hours ago: Russian Army Intercepts Over 1.2K Ukrainian Drones in Latest Nighttime Air Barrage.
Regional authorities said at least three people were killed in strikes across the country over the past day.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Strikes on oil refineries cut Russian diesel sales threefold.
Diesel sales on Russian commodity exchanges plunged by 67% and petrol sales fell by 33% in late November as drone attacks forced major refinery shutdowns.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Ukrainian forces strike Russian Rubicon drone unit's base in occupied Berdiansk.
Ukrainian forces struck a Russian Rubicon drone unit base in occupied Berdiansk, with early reports indicating over 30 Russians killed and up to 70 wounded.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Zelenskyy wants Crimean Bridge completely destroyed, new strikes being prepared – The Telegraph.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has told Ukraine's military command he wants the Crimean Bridge completely destroyed, with new strikes being prepared.
Southern Europe - bottom line: We’d be ‘stupid’ not to: Poland defends $300M military AI deal with Palantir.
- Politico Europe, one day ago: We’d be ‘stupid’ not to: Poland defends $300M military AI deal with Palantir.
Poland's defense minister said it would be “wrong” not to use the software, despite concerns over reliance on American technology.
- Balkan Insight, one day ago: Democracy Digest: V4 Remain Critical of Budget as EU Summit Ends Without Deal.
Elsewhere, Ukrainian youth in hospital after setting himself on fire opposite Warsaw’s presidential palace; postal voting scrapped for Slovakia’s 2027 election; EU Parliament warns against Czechia’s public media reforms.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Saudi coalition shoots down Houthi cruise missile fired toward Riyadh.
- Africanews, 4 hours ago: Saudi coalition shoots down Houthi cruise missile fired toward Riyadh.
The news comes as Houthi-run media in Yemen said at least 15 people were injured in Saudi airstrikes on a residential area of Sanaa.
- Africanews, 23 hours ago: Cairo mourns 31 victims of deadly fuel tanker inferno as families bid farewell.
Grief and shock have gripped Cairo's Waraq district as families and residents gathered to mourn victims of Wednesday's deadly fuel tanker inferno.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Pompeo predicts US blockade will push Iran to escalate, reigniting Israel, US strikes on regime.
- Jerusalem Post, 4 hours ago: Pompeo predicts US blockade will push Iran to escalate, reigniting Israel, US strikes on regime.
Pompeo said the US should hit Iran's industrial base, missiles, and drones and "go after the next set of leaders" to end the war.
- Jerusalem Post, 17 hours ago: IDF kills two Hamas terrorists who also worked for Doctors Without Borders, military says.
Doctors Without Borders condemns the IDF strike that killed Hamas terrorists working at an MSF clinic, calling for accountability, claiming it was a "direct attack on MSF."
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Iran points to Europe’s war role after Italians killed in Kuwait strike.
Italy and Kuwait say an Iranian drone was involved, but Tehran says the US and Israel may be looking to escalate war.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, just now: Russia and Ukraine strike energy infrastructure, as attacks kill 10.
Russia-Ukraine attacks have become more regular and hybrid, as the fifth anniversary of invasion approaches.
South Africa - bottom line: Nigeria: Why Nigerians in South Africa Welcome an Envoy Who Refuses to Whisper.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: Nigeria: Why Nigerians in South Africa Welcome an Envoy Who Refuses to Whisper.
[Daily Trust] When big men rise, little men tremble. When a patriot that truly cares about the welfare and safety of his people comes on the scene, the cowards and traitors murmur. When light comes, darkness cries and inevitably flees.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: Zimbabwe: Police to Name and Shame Companies Selling Counterfeit Agricultural Inputs.
[New Zimbabwe] THE Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) has warned that it will name and shame backyard garages, unregistered companies and individuals involved in manufacturing and selling counterfeit agricultural inputs to farmers.

ASIA
India - bottom line: From school to wedding house: Myanmar military airstrikes leave over 35 civilians dead.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: From school to wedding house: Myanmar military airstrikes leave over 35 civilians dead.
A military airstrike in Myanmar resulted in the deaths of at least 30 individuals, including an infant and schoolchildren. The attack occurred during a religious ceremony in a rebel-controlled village and involved multiple aerial bombs. Opposition authorities condemned the action, calling it unprovoked and a potential war crime. Additionally, a separate airstrike during a wedding in another area killed several people, with witnesses reporting chaos.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: At Least 30 Killed In Three Separate Military Airstrikes In Myanmar.
A strike on a wedding venue in Moe Bye district in the northeast saw around 20 people killed, according to witnesses, with multiple fatalities in two separate bombings in western Rakhine state.
- Times of India - Top Stories, The Hindu - International, South China Morning Post - China, AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 2 hours ago: At least 9 civilians killed in Ukraine as Russia claims near-record drone interceptions.
At least nine civilians died in recent drone strikes in Ukraine, including a Russian attack in Nizhyn. Rescue operations concluded after seven casualties were reported in a Russian assault on a local business. In Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia, a Ukrainian drone strike killed two people near a hospital vehicle. Additionally, Ukraine’s Air Force successfully intercepted numerous Russian drones launched overnight. Both sides are intensifying targeted strikes on critical infrastructure in ongoing conflict.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Michigan neighbours' dock dispute ends with permanent ban and $1 trespass award.
A Michigan couple's six-year dispute with their neighbour over a dock extending across an underwater property boundary has ended with an appeals court upholding a permanent ban on the structure. The court also retained a $1 trespass award after rejecting the couple's arguments that their claimed rights as lakeside property owners allowed them to use the disputed area.
South Asia - bottom line: Airstrike on Myanmar wedding venue kills around 20, say witnesses.
- The Hindu - International, South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Airstrike on Myanmar wedding venue kills around 20, say witnesses.
Myanmar has been in the throes of civil war since a coup deposed Aung San Suu Kyi's elected government in 2021, and monitoring group ACLED says more than 100,000 people have been killed on all sides
- The Hindu - International, 11 hours ago: Saudi Arabia, Houthis trade attacks on rival capitals.
A Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government has been regularly bombing areas controlled by the Iran-backed group since Yemen's civil war reignited over the summer
- The Hindu - International, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Putin unveils new nuclear submarine.
Nuclear-powered submarines are a key part of Russia's nuclear deterrent because their ability to operate covertly underwater ensures a retaliatory strike capability in the event of an attack
- The Hindu - International, one hour ago: Somali pirates hijack UAE ship from Yemen, say security officials.
Piracy has seen a resurgence in the waters off the Horn of Africa, with at least 16 attacks since April, the highest level since 2013
Asia - bottom line: US Navy pushes ahead with submarine-launched nuclear cruise missile programme.
- South China Morning Post - China, 7 hours ago: US Navy pushes ahead with submarine-launched nuclear cruise missile programme.
The United States is a step closer to restoring atomic weapons to its attack submarines, with Raytheon announcing on Tuesday it has a US Navy deal to advance development of a nuclear-armed cruise missile – a capability Washington retired in 2013. The agreement will see Raytheon – one of several defence contractors working on competing designs – move its existing missile concept into a “focused development phase”. Once operational, such a weapon could give Washington additional regional...
- South China Morning Post - China, 10 hours ago: Teary-eyed fiancée, brother of firefighter Ho Wai-ho receive posthumous medal.
Tears welled up in the eyes of the fiancée of firefighter Ho Wai-ho, who was killed in the city’s deadliest blaze in decades, as she joined his brother on Saturday to accept a posthumous bravery medal from Hong Kong’s leader, days after the first anniversary of the inferno. Ho, 37, was awarded the Medal for Bravery (Gold) in the 2026 Honours List for his “act of the most conspicuous courage, selflessness and bravery” during last November’s Tai Po fire, which claimed 168 lives and displaced about...
- South China Morning Post - China, 9 hours ago: Scientists find dice, game tiles in Kublai Khan shipwreck, revealing how troops coped at sea.
When Mongol leader Kublai Khan launched one of the largest naval invasions in human history in 1281, he was seeking a place to resettle a defeated Chinese army – and Japan was in his sights. But conquering Japan proved a vexing challenge for Kublai Khan’s military ambitions, and a typhoon sent the massive armada to the bottom of the sea. A campaign intended to cement the overthrow of China’s Southern Song dynasty (1127–1279) would become a rallying cry in Japan for centuries. A recent discovery...
- South China Morning Post - China, 19 hours ago: Son of Hamas chief survived Israeli strike, group says.
The son of Hamas ⁠chief Khalil al-Hayya survived an assassination attempt ⁠by the Israeli military on Friday, senior Hamas official ⁠Basem Naim said. He said that Izzeldeen al-Hayya and his family had survived a dawn air strike and Hamas sources said several people, including Hayya’s daughter-in-law, had been wounded but there had been no deaths. The Israeli military had no immediate comment. Naim described Izzeldeen al-Hayya, born in 1997, as the Hamas chief’s last surviving son, with four...
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: (2nd LD) Lee vows all-out efforts to lead AI race at data center groundbreaking in Gangwon.
- Yonhap News Agency, 12 hours ago: (2nd LD) Lee vows all-out efforts to lead AI race at data center groundbreaking in Gangwon.
SEOUL, Nov. 28 (Yonhap) -- President Lee Jae Myung pledged Saturday to mobilize ...
- Yonhap News Agency, 16 hours ago: Internet Post Office hacked; personal data of at least 113,000 customers leaked.
SEOUL, Nov. 28 (Yonhap) -- A hacking attack on the Internet Post Office has expo...

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Israeli air strike on Doctors Without Borders Gaza office kills two.
- ABC News Australia, The Hindu - International, 7 hours ago: Israeli air strike on Doctors Without Borders Gaza office kills two.
The World Health Organization condemns attacks on health facilities after an Israeli air strike on an MSF building in Gaza killed two people.
- ABC News Australia, South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 7 hours ago: Explosion at Afghanistan school kills seven students, wounds 97 people.
An explosion at a school in Afghanistan has killed seven students and wounded more than 90 people, officials say.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: The inside story of how an ASIO shake-up may have changed the odds on Bondi.
ASIO boss Mike Burgess was hired to drag Australia's domestic spy agency into the modern era. Almost a year on from the Bondi terror attack, insiders are asking if the organisations turn to tech and foreign spies as veteran officers quit let vital information slip through the gaps.
